title: interface node
description:
What a context publishes or consumes. A `domain-event` is something that happened inside a context, named in the past tense; an `integration-event` crosses a context boundary and is therefore a published contract someone else depends on; a `published-language` is a shared vocabulary for exchange; an `api` is an exposed operation.

Whether the context publishes or consumes decides who owes whom compatibility. A break requires a version bump and a migration, from which a consumed interface is exempt.

An interface is also the only target a reference crossing a bounded context may name.

schema.description: Where the machine-readable payload contract lives. The form of this value is not closed.

x-alternation: Everything this kind requires, or a declared gap naming what is missing. A prohibition is not excused: a gap says a fact is absent and cannot make a forbidden field allowed.
